MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. 75 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 0.07
   B. Ksh 0.75
   C. Ksh 1.75
   D. Ksh 7.50

2. 2,005 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 20.05
   B. Ksh 21.05
   C. Ksh 200.50
   D. Ksh 2

3. Which is the same as half a shilling? (1 mark)
   A. 50 cents
   B. 10 cents
   C. 500 cents
   D. 5 cents

4. One unit costs Ksh 15. What is the cost of 12 pencils? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 27
   B. Ksh 165
   C. Ksh 180
   D. Ksh 190

5. A customer pays with Ksh 500 for goods that cost Ksh 235. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 365
   B. Ksh 255
   C. Ksh 265
   D. Ksh 735

6. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 240, Ksh 160 and Ksh 350. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 760
   B. Ksh 650
   C. Ksh 850
   D. Ksh 750

7. A customer pays with Ksh 5,000 for goods that cost Ksh 3,350. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 8,350
   B. Ksh 1,650
   C. Ksh 1,750
   D. Ksh 1,640

8. Kip faces North and makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. East
   C. South
   D. West

9. Kip faces North and makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. South
   C. North
   D. East

10. Kip faces North and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. West
   C. South
   D. East

11. Which object does NOT have a right angle at its corners? (1 mark)
   A. A book
   B. A door
   C. A round plate
   D. A window

12. How many right angles make a full turn? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 4
   C. 2
   D. 1

13. How many right angles are there in a rectangle? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 4
   C. 2
   D. 3

14. In the pattern blue square, orange square, blue square, orange square, and so on, what colour is the 6th square? (1 mark)
   A. Red
   B. Blue
   C. Green
   D. Orange

15. What is the fold line that divides a shape into two matching halves called? (1 mark)
   A. A perimeter
   B. An angle
   C. A line of symmetry
   D. A vertex

16. Which of these letters has a line of symmetry? (1 mark)
   A. H
   B. R
   C. G
   D. F

17. What is raw data? (1 mark)
   A. A picture of data
   B. Data that has been collected but not yet arranged
   C. Data that is wrong
   D. Data written in a table

18. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. How many are football or swimming together? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 7
   C. 5
   D. 6

19. Which is a good tool for drawing straight lines in a table? (1 mark)
   A. A measuring jug
   B. A clock
   C. A ruler
   D. A beam balance

20. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many are NOT car? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 11
   C. 9
   D. 10

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A shopkeeper counts up to give change. A customer buys goods for Ksh 750 and pays with Ksh 1,000. Show how the shopkeeper counts up. (3 marks)

22. Describe how you can use a folded piece of paper to test whether a corner is a right angle. (3 marks)

23. Describe a pattern of shapes that you can make with squares and triangles, and write down the first six shapes. (3 marks)

24. Njeri faces east. She makes two quarter turns clockwise, one after the other. Which way does she face? (3 marks)

25. Amina faces north. She makes a half turn, then a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does she face at the end? (4 marks)

26. Explain why we add the numbers in the total row of a table. (3 marks)

27. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. (a) How many lines of symmetry does it have? (b) How many right angles does it have? (c) Find its perimeter. (d) Say one way in which it is different from a square. (5 marks)

28. Draw a rectangle 6 cm long and 3 cm wide and label its sides. (3 marks)

29. A sweet costs 50 cents. How many sweets can be bought with Ksh 10? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Ksh 0.75
   75 ÷ 100 = 0 remainder 75, so it is Ksh 0.75.

2. A — Ksh 20.05
   2,005 ÷ 100 = 20 remainder 5, so it is Ksh 20.05.

3. A — 50 cents
   One shilling is 100 cents, so half a shilling is 50 cents.

4. C — Ksh 180
   Cost = number × price = 12 × 15 = Ksh 180.

5. C — Ksh 265
   Change = amount paid − cost = 500 − 235 = Ksh 265.

6. D — Ksh 750
   Add the three costs: 240 + 160 + 350 = 750.

7. B — Ksh 1,650
   Change = amount paid − cost = 5,000 − 3,350 = Ksh 1,650.

8. D — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a three-quarter turn clockwise gives West.

9. A — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a quarter turn anticlockwise gives West.

10. D — East
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a quarter turn clockwise gives East.

11. C — A round plate
   A round plate has a curved edge and no corners, so no right angles.

12. B — 4
   A full turn is four quarter turns, and each quarter turn is a right angle.

13. B — 4
   A rectangle has four corners and each is a right angle.

14. D — Orange
   The colours alternate blue, orange. Squares 2, 4 and 6 are orange.

15. C — A line of symmetry
   If the two halves match exactly, the fold is a line of symmetry.

16. A — H
   The letter H can be folded down the middle and the halves match.

17. B — Data that has been collected but not yet arranged
   Raw data is untidy information straight from collection.

18. D — 6
   5 + 1 = 6.

19. C — A ruler
   A ruler is used to draw straight lines.

20. C — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: From 750 to 800 is 50, and from 800 to 1,000 is 200. Change = 50 + 200 = Ksh 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for counting to 800, 1 mark for counting to 1,000, 1 mark for adding to make Ksh 250.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fold a paper twice to make a neat square corner. Place its corner on the corner of the object. If it fits exactly, the corner is a right angle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for folding to make a square corner, 1 mark for placing it on the corner, 1 mark for saying it fits exactly.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: square, triangle, square, triangle, square, triangle. The pattern repeats a square and a triangle in turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using both shapes, 1 mark for a clear repeating rule, 1 mark for six correct shapes.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: West
   Working / marking points: First turn east to south (1 mark); second turn south to west (1 mark); answer west (1 mark).

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: East
   Working / marking points: A half turn from north gives south (2 marks). A quarter turn anticlockwise from south gives east (2 marks).

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: To check that we have counted everything and that the total equals the number of items collected. If it is different we must count again.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for checking, 1 mark for comparing with the number collected, 1 mark for counting again.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 2 (b) 4 (c) 26 cm (d) Its sides are not all equal (only opposite sides are equal), and it has 2 lines of symmetry instead of 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 2 marks for (c) (8 + 5 + 8 + 5 with the answer and unit), 1 mark for (d).

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: A rectangle with two sides 6 cm and two sides 3 cm and square corners.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four straight sides with square corners, 1 mark for correct lengths, 1 mark for labels.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20 sweets
   Working / marking points: Ksh 10 = 1,000 cents (1 mark); 1,000 ÷ 50 (1 mark); 20 sweets (1 mark).
